report.summary: Checkout-service experienced a 1.6× increase in resident memory and logged multiple OutOfMemoryError and GC overhead warnings during the 3‑hour investigation window.

likely_causes.title: Memory leak in checkout-service application code
likely_causes.rationale: Repeated OOM errors and sustained high GC overhead indicate that objects are accumulating in the heap beyond the configured limit.

supporting_evidence.detail: process_resident_memory_bytes rose from 758.35 MiB to 1230.43 MiB (1.6× increase) during the window.
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space logged 4 times between 2026-09-23T11:53:46+00:00 and 2026-09-23T12:14:46+00:00.
GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92% logged 16 times between 2026-09-23T10:59:46+00:00 and 2026-09-23T12:14:46+00:00.

likely_causes.title: Insufficient Java heap size configuration
likely_causes.rationale: Heap usage reached 92% and OOM errors occurred, suggesting the JVM heap size may be too small for the workload.

supporting_evidence.detail: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space logged 4 times during the window.
GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92% logged 16 times during the window.

next_steps: Collect and analyze heap dumps from the affected instances to identify retained objects.
Review recent code changes or deployments for new allocations or data structures.
Increase the JVM heap size (e.g., -Xmx) and monitor if memory usage stabilizes.
Implement application‑level memory profiling to detect leaks early.
